title: JEE Main 2026 · 24 Jan · Shift 2 (recreated)

qs.stem: Let P = [p<sub>ij</sub>] and Q = [q<sub>ij</sub>] be two square matrices of order 3 such that q<sub>ij</sub> = 2<sup>(i+j−1)</sup> p<sub>ij</sub> and det(Q) = 2<sup>10</sup>. Then the value of det(adj(adj P)) is :
steps: Since q<sub>ij</sub> = 2<sup>i</sup>·2<sup>j−1</sup>p<sub>ij</sub>, Q = D<sub>1</sub>PD<sub>2</sub> with D<sub>1</sub> = diag(2, 2<sup>2</sup>, 2<sup>3</sup>) and D<sub>2</sub> = diag(1, 2, 2<sup>2</sup>).
So |Q| = 2<sup>6</sup>·2<sup>3</sup>·|P| = 2<sup>9</sup>|P| = 2<sup>10</sup>, giving |P| = 2.
For order 3, |adj A| = |A|<sup>2</sup>, so |adj(adj P)| = |P|<sup>4</sup> = 2<sup>4</sup> = 16.

qs.stem: Let f(x) = ∫ (7x<sup>10</sup> + 9x<sup>8</sup>)/(1 + x<sup>2</sup> + 2x<sup>9</sup>)<sup>2</sup> dx, x > 0, lim<sub>x→0</sub> f(x) = 0 and f(1) = 1/4. If A = [[0, 0, 1], [1/4, f′(1), 1], [α<sup>2</sup>, 4, 1]] and B = adj(adj A) be such that |B| = 81, then α<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: Divide numerator and denominator by x<sup>18</sup>: with t = x<sup>−9</sup> + x<sup>−7</sup> + 2, dt = −(9x<sup>−10</sup> + 7x<sup>−8</sup>)dx, so the integral is 1/t + C = x<sup>9</sup>/(1 + x<sup>2</sup> + 2x<sup>9</sup>) + C; the limit at 0 gives C = 0 (and f(1) = 1/4 checks).
f′(1) = (9·4 − 1·20)/4<sup>2</sup> = 1.
Expanding along the first row, |A| = 1·(1/4·4 − 1·α<sup>2</sup>) = 1 − α<sup>2</sup>.
|B| = |A|<sup>4</sup> = 81 gives |A| = ±3. 1 − α<sup>2</sup> = 3 is impossible, so 1 − α<sup>2</sup> = −3 and α<sup>2</sup> = 4.

qs.stem: (1/3 + 4/7) + (1/3<sup>2</sup> + (1/3)(4/7) + 4<sup>2</sup>/7<sup>2</sup>) + (1/3<sup>3</sup> + (1/3<sup>2</sup>)(4/7) + (1/3)(4<sup>2</sup>/7<sup>2</sup>) + 4<sup>3</sup>/7<sup>3</sup>) + … up to infinite terms, is equal to :
steps: Put a = 1/3, b = 4/7. The n-th bracket is a<sup>n</sup> + a<sup>n−1</sup>b + … + b<sup>n</sup> = (a<sup>n+1</sup> − b<sup>n+1</sup>)/(a − b).
Sum over n ≥ 1: [a<sup>2</sup>/(1−a) − b<sup>2</sup>/(1−b)]/(a − b) = (a + b − ab)/((1−a)(1−b)).
a + b − ab = 1/3 + 4/7 − 4/21 = 15/21 = 5/7 and (1−a)(1−b) = (2/3)(3/7) = 2/7, so the sum is 5/2.

qs.stem: Let a1, a2, a3, a4 be an A.P. of four terms such that each term of the A.P. and its common difference l are integers. If a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 = 48 and a1a2a3a4 + l4 = 361, then the largest term of the A.P. is equal to :
steps: Write the terms as 12 − 3d, 12 − d, 12 + d, 12 + 3d (mean 12), so l = 2d.
Product = (144 − 9d2)(144 − d2) = 1442 − 1440d2 + 9d4; adding l4 = 16d4 gives 25d4 − 1440d2 + 20736 = 361.
25d4 − 1440d2 + 20375 = 0 has d2 = 25 (the other root 32.6 makes l irrational). So d = ±5 and the terms are 27, 17, 7, −3; the largest is 27.

qs.stem: Let the angles made with the positive x-axis by two straight lines drawn from the point P(2, 3) and meeting the line x + y = 6 at a distance √(2/3) from the point P be θ<sub>1</sub> and θ<sub>2</sub>. Then the value of (θ<sub>1</sub> + θ<sub>2</sub>) is :
steps: A point at distance r = ±√(2/3) along direction θ is (2 + r cosθ, 3 + r sinθ). On x + y = 6: 5 + r(cosθ + sinθ) = 6.
So (sinθ + cosθ)<sup>2</sup> = 3/2, i.e. sin 2θ = 1/2, i.e. 2tanθ/(1 + tan<sup>2</sup>θ) = 1/2, giving tan<sup>2</sup>θ − 4tanθ + 1 = 0.

The two slopes satisfy tanθ<sub>1</sub> + tanθ<sub>2</sub> = 4 and tanθ<sub>1</sub>tanθ<sub>2</sub> = 1, so tan(θ<sub>1</sub> + θ<sub>2</sub>) is infinite: θ<sub>1</sub> + θ<sub>2</sub> = π/2 (indeed θ = π/12 and 5π/12).

qs.stem:
Consider the following three statements for the function f : (0, ∞) → R defined by f(x) = |loge x| − |x − 1|
(I) f is differentiable at all x > 0.
(II) f is increasing in (0, 1).
(III) f is decreasing in (1, ∞) then :
steps: For 0 < x < 1: f = −ln x + x − 1, f′ = 1 − 1/x < 0. For x ≥ 1: f = ln x − x + 1, f′ = 1/x − 1 ≤ 0.
At x = 1 both one-sided derivatives are 0, so f is differentiable everywhere: (I) true.
f′ < 0 on (0, 1) so f is decreasing there: (II) false. f′ < 0 on (1, ∞): (III) true.

qs.stem: If the domain of the function f(x) = sin<sup>−1</sup>(1/(x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 2)) is (−∞, α] ∪ [β, γ] ∪ [δ, ∞) then α + β + γ + δ is equal to :
steps: Need |x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 2| ≥ 1 (the expression is nonzero automatically).
Case x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 2 ≥ 1: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 3 ≥ 0, so x ≤ −1 or x ≥ 3.
Case x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 2 ≤ −1: x<sup>2</sup> − 2x − 1 ≤ 0, so 1 − √2 ≤ x ≤ 1 + √2.
Domain = (−∞, −1] ∪ [1 − √2, 1 + √2] ∪ [3, ∞); the sum is −1 + (1 − √2) + (1 + √2) + 3 = 4.

qs.stem: The letters of the word "UDAYPUR" are written in all possible ways with or without meaning and these words are arranged as in a dictionary. The rank of the word "UDAYPUR" is :
steps: Alphabetical order of letters: A, D, P, R, U, U, Y. Words starting with A, D, P or R: 4 × 6!/2! = 1440.
Starting with U, second letter before D: UA… gives 5! = 120. Then UDA with fourth letter before Y (P, R, U): 3 × 3! = 18.
UDAY then P: no smaller; UDAYP then sixth letter before U: R gives 1 word (UDAYPRU).
Words before UDAYPUR = 1440 + 120 + 18 + 1 = 1579, so the rank is 1580.

qs.stem: Let the image of the parabola x<sup>2</sup> = 4y, in the line x − y = 1 be (y + a)<sup>2</sup> = b(x − c), a, b, c ∈ N. Then a + b + c is equal to :
steps: Reflection in x − y = 1 sends (x, y) to (y + 1, x − 1).
A point (2t, t<sup>2</sup>) of the parabola goes to X = t<sup>2</sup> + 1, Y = 2t − 1.
Eliminate t = (Y + 1)/2: X − 1 = (Y + 1)<sup>2</sup>/4, i.e. (y + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 4(x − 1).
So a = 1, b = 4, c = 1 and a + b + c = 6.

qs.stem: The largest value of n, for which 40<sup>n</sup> divides 60!, is :
steps: 40<sup>n</sup> = 2<sup>3n</sup>·5<sup>n</sup>.
Need n ≤ 14 and 3n ≤ 56 (n ≤ 18), so the largest n is 14.

qs.stem: Let X = {x ∈ N : 1 ≤ x ≤ 19} and for some a, b ∈ R, Y = {ax + b : x ∈ X}. If the mean and variance of the elements of Y are 30 and 750, respectively, then the sum of all possible values of b is :
steps: For X = 1..19: mean = 10 and variance = (19<sup>2</sup> − 1)/12 = 30.
Y has mean 10a + b = 30 and variance 30a<sup>2</sup> = 750, so a = ±5.
a = 5 gives b = −20; a = −5 gives b = 80. Sum of b values = 60.

qs.stem: Let [t] denote the greatest integer less than or equal to t. If the function f(x) = b<sup>2</sup> sin((π/2)[(π/2)(cos x + sin x) cos x]) for x < 0; (sin x − (1/2) sin 2x)/x<sup>3</sup> for x > 0; a for x = 0, is continuous at x = 0, then a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: Right limit: sin x − (1/2)sin 2x = (x − x<sup>3</sup>/6) − (x − 4x<sup>3</sup>/3) + … = x<sup>3</sup>/2 + …, so a = 1/2.
Left side: for small x < 0, (cos x + sin x)cos x is just below 1, so (π/2) times it lies just below π/2 ≈ 1.57, whose floor is 1.
Then f(x) → b<sup>2</sup> sin(π/2) = b<sup>2</sup>. Continuity: b<sup>2</sup> = 1/2.

qs.stem: The smallest positive integral value of a, for which all the roots of x<sup>4</sup> − ax<sup>2</sup> + 9 = 0 are real and distinct, is equal to :
steps: With t = x<sup>2</sup>: t<sup>2</sup> − at + 9 = 0 must have two distinct positive roots (then x = ±√t give four real distinct roots).
Distinct: a<sup>2</sup> − 36 > 0. Positive sum: a > 0. Product 9 > 0 already holds.
So a > 6 and the smallest integer is 7.

qs.stem: Let the length of the latus rectum of an ellipse x<sup>2</sup>/a<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/b<sup>2</sup> = 1, (a > b), be 30. If its eccentricity is the maximum value of the function f(t) = −3/4 + 2t − t<sup>2</sup>, then (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>) is equal to :
steps: f(t) = 1/4 − (t − 1)<sup>2</sup>, so the maximum is 1/4 and e = 1/4.
Latus rectum 2b<sup>2</sup>/a = 30 gives b<sup>2</sup> = 15a. Also b<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>(1 − e<sup>2</sup>) = 15a<sup>2</sup>/16.

qs.stem: The sum of all values of α, for which the shortest distance between the lines (x + 1)/α = (y − 2)/(−1) = (z − 4)/(−α) and x/α = (y − 1)/2 = (z − 1)/(2α) is √2, is :
steps: Directions d<sub>1</sub> = (α, −1, −α), d<sub>2</sub> = (α, 2, 2α); d<sub>1</sub> × d<sub>2</sub> = (0, −3α<sup>2</sup>, 3α). Vector between points (−1, 2, 4) and (0, 1, 1) is (1, −1, −3).
Dot product = 3α<sup>2</sup> − 9α; modulus of the cross product = 3|α|√(α<sup>2</sup> + 1).
Distance = |α − 3|/√(α<sup>2</sup> + 1) = √2, so (α − 3)<sup>2</sup> = 2α<sup>2</sup> + 2, i.e. α<sup>2</sup> + 6α − 7 = 0.
α = 1 or −7 (α = 0 gives parallel lines at distance √10, rejected). Sum = −6.

qs.stem: Let f be a function such that 3f(x) + 2f(m/(19x)) = 5x, x ≠ 0, where m = ∑<sub>i=1</sub><sup>9</sup> (i)<sup>2</sup>. Then f(5) − f(2) is equal to :
steps: m = 9·10·19/6 = 285, so m/19 = 15 and the relation is 3f(x) + 2f(15/x) = 5x.
x = 2 and x = 15/2: 3f(2) + 2f(7.5) = 10 and 3f(7.5) + 2f(2) = 37.5. Eliminating gives 5f(2) = −45, f(2) = −9.

qs.stem: Let y = y(x) be a differentiable function in the interval (0, ∞) such that y(1) = 2, and lim<sub>t→x</sub> (t<sup>2</sup>y(x) − x<sup>2</sup>y(t))/(x − t) = 3 for each x > 0. Then 2y(2) is equal to :
steps: The limit is a 0/0 form; differentiating numerator and denominator in t: (2ty(x) − x<sup>2</sup>y′(t))/(−1) at t = x gives x<sup>2</sup>y′ − 2xy = 3.
So y′ − (2/x)y = 3/x<sup>2</sup>; integrating factor 1/x<sup>2</sup>: d(y/x<sup>2</sup>)/dx = 3/x<sup>4</sup>, so y/x<sup>2</sup> = −1/x<sup>3</sup> + c.
y(1) = 2 gives c = 3, so y = 3x<sup>2</sup> − 1/x.

qs.stem: Let a = 2i − 5j + 5k and b = i − j + 3k. If c is a vector such that 2(a × c) + 3(b × c) = 0 and (a − b)·c = −97, then |c × k|2 is equal to :
steps: The first condition says (2a + 3b) × c = 0, so c = λ(2a + 3b) = λ(7, −13, 19).
a − b = (1, −4, 2), and (a − b)·(7, −13, 19) = 7 + 52 + 38 = 97, so 97λ = −97, λ = −1 and c = (−7, 13, −19).
|c × k|2 = cx2 + cy2 = 49 + 169 = 218.

qs.stem: Let f(α) denote the area of the region in the first quadrant bounded by x = 0, x = 1, y<sup>2</sup> = x and y = |αx − 5| − |1 − αx| + αx<sup>2</sup>. Then (f(0) + f(1)) is equal to :
steps: α = 0: y = 5 − 1 = 4. Area = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup>(4 − √x)dx = 4 − 2/3 = 10/3.
α = 1: for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, y = (5 − x) − (1 − x) + x<sup>2</sup> = 4 + x<sup>2</sup>. Area = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup>(4 + x<sup>2</sup> − √x)dx = 4 + 1/3 − 2/3 = 11/3.

qs.stem: Let (h, k) lie on the circle C : x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 4 and the point (2h + 1, 3k + 2) lie on an ellipse with eccentricity e. Then the value of 5/e<sup>2</sup> is equal to ______.
steps: Let x = 2h + 1, y = 3k + 2, so h = (x − 1)/2 and k = (y − 2)/3.
h<sup>2</sup> + k<sup>2</sup> = 4 becomes (x − 1)<sup>2</sup>/16 + (y − 2)<sup>2</sup>/36 = 1, an ellipse with semi-axes 4 and 6.
e<sup>2</sup> = 1 − 16/36 = 5/9, so 5/e<sup>2</sup> = 9.

qs.stem: The number of elements in the set {x ∈ [0, 180°] : tan(x + 100°) = tan(x + 50°) tan x tan(x − 50°)} is ______.
steps: Write as tan(x + 100°)/tan(x − 50°) = tan(x + 50°)tan x, expand every tangent as sin/cos and use product-to-sum on each of the four products.
Componendo-dividendo then reduces it to sin(2x + 50°)cos(2x + 50°) = −(1/2)cos 50°, i.e. sin(4x + 100°) = −cos 50° = sin(−40°).
With 4x + 100° in [100°, 820°]: 4x + 100° = 220°, 320°, 580°, 680°, giving x = 30°, 55°, 120°, 145°.
All four keep every tangent defined, so the set has 4 elements.

qs.stem: Let z = (1 + i)(1 + 2i)(1 + 3i) … (1 + ni), where i = √−1. If |z|<sup>2</sup> = 44200, then n is equal to ______.
steps: Running products: 2, 10, 100, 1700, 44200 for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (2·5·10·17·26 = 44200).
Hence n = 5.

qs.stem: Let S be a set of 5 elements and P(S) denote the power set of S. Let E be an event of choosing an ordered pair (A, B) from the set P(S) × P(S) such that A ∩ B = ∅. If the probability of the event E is 3<sup>p</sup>/2<sup>q</sup>, where p, q ∈ N, then p + q is equal to ______.
steps: Total ordered pairs = 32 × 32 = 2<sup>10</sup>.
For disjoint A, B each element lies in A only, B only or neither: 3 choices, so 3<sup>5</sup> pairs.
Probability = 3<sup>5</sup>/2<sup>10</sup>, so p = 5, q = 10 and p + q = 15.

qs.stem: If f(x) satisfies the relation f(x) = e<sup>x</sup> + ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> (y + xe<sup>x</sup>) f(y) dy, then e + f(0) is equal to ______.
steps: Let λ = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> f(y)dy and μ = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> y f(y)dy. Then f(x) = e<sup>x</sup> + λxe<sup>x</sup> + μ.
Integrate f over [0, 1]: λ = (e − 1) + λ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> ye<sup>y</sup>dy + μ = (e − 1) + λ·1 + μ, so μ = 1 − e.
f(0) = 1 + μ = 2 − e, hence e + f(0) = 2.

qs.stem: A moving coil galvanometer of resistance 100Ω shows a full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. The value of resistance required to convert this galvanometer into an ammeter, showing full scale deflection for a current of 5 mA, is ________ Ω.
steps: The galvanometer must carry only 1 mA, so the shunt R carries 5 − 1 = 4 mA.
The shunt is in parallel with the coil, so the voltages match: 4 mA × R = 1 mA × 100 Ω.

qs.stem: When a light of a given wavelength falls on a metallic surface the stopping potential for photoelectrons is 3.2 V. If a second light having wavelength twice of first light is used, the stopping potential drops to 0.7 V. The wavelength of first light is ________ m. (h = 6.63×10<sup>−34</sup> J.s, e = 1.6×10<sup>−19</sup> C, c = 3×10<sup>8</sup> m/s)
steps: Einstein: hc/λ = φ + e(3.2) and hc/(2λ) = φ + e(0.7).
Subtract: hc/(2λ) = e(3.2 − 0.7) = 2.5e, so hc/λ = 5e.
λ = hc/(5e) = (6.63×10<sup>−34</sup> × 3×10<sup>8</sup>)/(5 × 1.6×10<sup>−19</sup>) = 1.989×10<sup>−25</sup>/8×10<sup>−19</sup> ≈ 2.5×10<sup>−7</sup> m.

qs.stem: In a vernier callipers, 50 vernier scale divisions are equal to 48 main scale divisions. If one main scale division = 0.05 mm, then the least count of the vernier callipers is ______ mm.
steps: 1 VSD = (48/50) MSD, so least count = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = (2/50) MSD.

qs.stem: Three parallel plate capacitors each with area A and separation d are filled with two dielectrics (k<sub>1</sub> and k<sub>2</sub>) in the following fashion (see figure). Which of the following is true? (k<sub>1</sub> > k<sub>2</sub>)
steps: Work in units of ε<sub>0</sub>A/d. A layer of thickness d/2 with k over the full area gives 2k; a half-area, half-thickness block with k gives k.

(A): top layer 2k<sub>1</sub> in series with (k<sub>1</sub> + k<sub>2</sub>) in parallel: C<sub>A</sub> = 2k<sub>1</sub>(k<sub>1</sub>+k<sub>2</sub>)/(3k<sub>1</sub>+k<sub>2</sub>). (B): C<sub>B</sub> = 2k<sub>2</sub>(k<sub>1</sub>+k<sub>2</sub>)/(k<sub>1</sub>+3k<sub>2</sub>). (C): two columns of k<sub>1</sub> and k<sub>2</sub> in series, in parallel: C<sub>C</sub> = 2k<sub>1</sub>k<sub>2</sub>/(k<sub>1</sub>+k<sub>2</sub>).
Check with k<sub>1</sub> = 2, k<sub>2</sub> = 1: C<sub>A</sub> = 12/7 ≈ 1.71, C<sub>C</sub> = 4/3 ≈ 1.33, C<sub>B</sub> = 6/5 = 1.2, so C<sub>A</sub> > C<sub>C</sub> > C<sub>B</sub>.

qs.stem: A flexible chain of mass m hangs between two fixed points at the same level. The inclination of the chain with the horizontal at the two points of support is 30°. Considering the equilibrium of each half of the chain, the tension of the chain at the lowest point is ________.
steps: Whole chain: vertical balance at the two supports gives 2T sin30° = mg, so T = mg at each support.
Half chain: horizontal balance gives the tension at the lowest point T' = T cos30°.
T' = mg × √3/2 = (√3/2) mg.

qs.stem: A thin uniform rod (X) of mass M and length L is pivoted at a height (L/3) as shown in the figure (the pivot is L/3 above the lower end of the vertical rod, at the table edge). The rod is allowed to fall from a vertical position and lie horizontally on the table. The angular velocity of this rod when it hits the table top, is ________. (g = gravitational acceleration)
steps: The centre of mass is L/2 − L/3 = L/6 above the pivot, so it falls by L/6 when the rod becomes horizontal.
Moment of inertia about the pivot: I = ML<sup>2</sup>/12 + M(L/6)<sup>2</sup> = ML<sup>2</sup>/9.
Energy: Mg(L/6) = (1/2)(ML<sup>2</sup>/9)ω<sup>2</sup>, so ω<sup>2</sup> = 3g/L and ω = √(3g/L).

qs.stem: Two identical circular loops P and Q each of radius r are lying in parallel planes such that they have common axis (their centres are a distance 2r apart, with O midway on the axis, so O is at distance r from each centre). The currents through P and Q are I and 4I respectively in clockwise direction as seen from O. The net magnetic field at O is :
steps: On the axis of a loop at distance x: B = μ<sub>0</sub>IR<sup>2</sup>/[2(R<sup>2</sup>+x<sup>2</sup>)<sup>3/2</sup>]. With R = x = r, B = μ<sub>0</sub>I/(4√2 r) for current I.
Both loops circulate clockwise as seen from O, so each field at O points along the axis away from the viewer, i.e. P's field points toward P and Q's toward Q: they oppose.
Net = (4 − 1) × μ<sub>0</sub>I/(4√2 r) = 3μ<sub>0</sub>I/(4√2 r), directed toward Q (the stronger loop).

qs.stem: A cubical block of density ρ<sub>b</sub> = 600 kg/m<sup>3</sup> floats in a liquid of density ρ<sub>e</sub> = 900 kg/m<sup>3</sup>. If the height of block is H = 8.0 cm then height of the submerged part is ________ cm.
steps: Floating: weight = buoyancy, so (submerged volume)/(total volume) = ρ<sub>b</sub>/ρ<sub>e</sub> = 600/900 = 2/3.
Same base area, so submerged height = (2/3) × 8.0 cm ≈ 5.3 cm.

qs.stem: Distance between an object and three times magnified real image is 40 cm. The focal length of the mirror used is ________ cm.
steps: A real, magnified image means a concave mirror with the object between f and 2f; |v| = 3|u| and |v| − |u| = 40, so |u| = 20 cm, |v| = 60 cm.
Mirror formula with real-is-negative signs: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u = −1/60 − 1/20 = −4/60.
f = −15 cm.

qs.stem: Five persons P<sub>1</sub>, P<sub>2</sub>, P<sub>3</sub>, P<sub>4</sub> and P<sub>5</sub> recorded object distance (u) and image distance (v) using same convex lens having power +5 D as (25, 96), (30, 62), (35, 37), (45, 35) and (50, 32) respectively. Identify correct statement
steps: P = +5 D gives f = 1/5 m = 20 cm.

Using magnitudes (real images), 1/f = 1/u + 1/v: P<sub>1</sub>: 1/25 + 1/96 gives f ≈ 19.8 cm; P<sub>2</sub>: 1/30 + 1/62 gives 20.2 cm; P<sub>4</sub>: 1/45 + 1/35 gives 19.7 cm; P<sub>5</sub>: 1/50 + 1/32 gives 19.5 cm.
P<sub>3</sub>: 1/35 + 1/37 gives f ≈ 18.0 cm, clearly off from 20 cm, so only P<sub>3</sub> is incorrect.
opts: Readings recorded by P<sub>4</sub> and P<sub>5</sub> persons are incorrect
Readings recorded by P<sub>3</sub> person are incorrect
Readings recorded by P<sub>3</sub> and P<sub>2</sub> persons are incorrect
Readings recorded by all persons are correct

qs.stem: A regular hexagon is formed by six wires each of resistance rΩ and the corners are joined to the centre by wires of same resistance. If the current enters at one corner and leaves at the opposite corner, the equivalent resistance of the hexagon between the two opposite corners will be
steps: Take r = 1, entry corner at potential 1, exit corner at 0. By antisymmetry the centre sits at 1/2 and the two neighbours of the entry corner share one potential V.
KCL at a neighbour: (1 − V) + (1 − 2V) + (1/2 − V) = 0, giving V = 5/8.
Current out of the entry corner = 2 × (3/8) + 1/2 = 5/4, so R = 1/(5/4) = 4/5, i.e. (4/5) r.

qs.stem: A point source is kept at the center of a spherically enclosed detector. If the volume of the detector increased by 8 times, the intensity will
steps: Intensity at the detector surface: I = P/(4πr<sup>2</sup>), so I ∝ 1/r<sup>2</sup>.
Volume ∝ r<sup>3</sup>; 8 times the volume means r doubles.
So the intensity falls to 1/4, i.e. it decreases by 4 times.

qs.stem: In the Young's double slit experiment the intensity produced by each one of the individual slits is I<sub>0</sub>. The distance between two slits is 2 mm. The distance of screen from slits is 10 m. The wavelength of light is 6000 Å. The intensity of light on the screen in front of one of the slits is ________.
steps: In front of one slit, y = d/2, so path difference Δ = yd/D = d<sup>2</sup>/(2D) = (4×10<sup>−6</sup>)/20 = 2×10<sup>−7</sup> m.
Phase difference φ = 2πΔ/λ = 2π × (2×10<sup>−7</sup>)/(6×10<sup>−7</sup>) = 2π/3.
I = 4I<sub>0</sub> cos<sup>2</sup>(φ/2) = 4I<sub>0</sub> cos<sup>2</sup>(π/3) = 4I<sub>0</sub> × 1/4 = I<sub>0</sub>.

qs.stem: The fifth harmonic of a closed organ pipe is found to be in unison with the first harmonic of an open pipe. The ratio of lengths of closed pipe to that of the open pipe is 5/x. The value of x is ________.
steps: Closed pipe has only odd harmonics: f = 5v/(4L<sub>c</sub>). Open pipe fundamental: f = v/(2L<sub>o</sub>).
Equate: 5/(4L<sub>c</sub>) = 1/(2L<sub>o</sub>), so L<sub>c</sub>/L<sub>o</sub> = 5/2.
Hence x = 2.

qs.stem: The binding energy for the following nuclear reactions are expressed in MeV. <sub>2</sub>He<sup>3</sup> + <sub>0</sub>n<sup>1</sup> → <sub>2</sub>He<sup>4</sup> + 20 MeV ; <sub>2</sub>He<sup>4</sup> + <sub>0</sub>n<sup>1</sup> → <sub>2</sub>He<sup>5</sup> − 0.9 MeV. If X<sub>3</sub>, X<sub>4</sub>, X<sub>5</sub> denote the stability of <sub>2</sub>He<sup>3</sup>, <sub>2</sub>He<sup>4</sup> and <sub>2</sub>He<sup>5</sup>, respectively, then the correct order is :
steps: Stability follows total binding energy. From the first reaction, BE(He-4) = BE(He-3) + 20 MeV, so He-4 is more stable than He-3.
From the second, BE(He-5) = BE(He-4) − 0.9 MeV = BE(He-3) + 19.1 MeV.
So BE(He-4) > BE(He-5) > BE(He-3), i.e. X<sub>4</sub> > X<sub>5</sub> > X<sub>3</sub>.

qs.stem: In case of vertical circular motion of a particle by a thread of length r if the tension in the thread is zero at an angle 30° (above the horizontal through the centre, as shown in the figure), the velocity at the bottom point (A) of the circular path is (g = gravitational acceleration)
steps: At the point 30° above the horizontal, the radial component of weight supplies the centripetal force (T = 0): mg sin30° = mv<sup>2</sup>/r, so v<sup>2</sup> = gr/2.
That point is higher than the bottom by r + r sin30° = 3r/2.
Energy: u<sup>2</sup> = v<sup>2</sup> + 2g(3r/2) = gr/2 + 3gr = 7gr/2, so u = √(7gr/2).
qs.fig: <svg viewBox='0 0 140 140' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' stroke='currentColor' fill='none' stroke-width='1.5' font-size='11'><circle cx='70' cy='70' r='55'/><line x1='70' y1='70' x2='117.6' y2='42.5' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><circle cx='117.6' cy='42.5' r='3' fill='currentColor'/><line x1='70' y1='70' x2='125' y2='70' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><line x1='70' y1='70' x2='70' y2='125'/><text x='96' y='66' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>30°</text><text x='74' y='100' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>r</text><text x='66' y='138' fill='currentColor' stroke='none'>A</text></svg>

qs.stem: A uniform solid cylinder of length L and radius R has moment of inertia about its axis equal to I<sub>1</sub>. A small co-centric cylinder of length L/2 and radius R/3 carved from this cylinder has moment of inertia about its axis equals to I<sub>2</sub>. The ratio I<sub>1</sub>/I<sub>2</sub> is
steps: I<sub>1</sub> = (1/2)MR<sup>2</sup> with M = ρπR<sup>2</sup>L, so I<sub>1</sub> = (1/2)ρπR<sup>4</sup>L.
Carved piece: mass m = ρπ(R/3)<sup>2</sup>(L/2) = M/18, so I<sub>2</sub> = (1/2)(M/18)(R/3)<sup>2</sup> = MR<sup>2</sup>/324.
I<sub>1</sub>/I<sub>2</sub> = (MR<sup>2</sup>/2)/(MR<sup>2</sup>/324) = 162.

qs.stem: A point charge q = 1μC is located at a distance 2 cm from one end of a thin insulating wire of length 10 cm having a charge Q = 24μC, distributed uniformly along its length, as shown in figure (the point charge lies on the line of the wire, beyond one end). Force between q and wire is ________ N. (Use: 1/(4πε<sub>0</sub>) = 9×10<sup>9</sup> N.m<sup>2</sup>/C<sup>2</sup>)
steps: Linear charge density λ = 24 μC/0.10 m = 2.4×10<sup>−4</sup> C/m. A strip dx at distance x gives dF = kqλ dx/x<sup>2</sup> (all along one line).
F = kqλ ∫<sub>0.02</sub><sup>0.12</sup> dx/x<sup>2</sup> = kqλ(1/0.02 − 1/0.12) = kqλ × 41.67.
kqλ = 9×10<sup>9</sup> × 10<sup>−6</sup> × 2.4×10<sup>−4</sup> = 2.16; F = 2.16 × 41.67 = 90 N.

qs.stem: In a meter bridge experiment to determine the value of unknown resistance, first the resistances 2Ω and 3Ω are connected in the left and right gaps of the bridge and the null point is obtained at a distance l cm from the left. Now when an unknown resistance xΩ is connected in parallel to 3Ω resistance, the null point is shifted by 10 cm to the right of wire. The value of unknown resistance x is ________ Ω.
steps: Balance condition: (left gap)/(right gap) = (length l)/(100 − l). First case: 2/3 = l/(100 − l), so l = 40 cm.
Now the null point is at 50 cm, so the length ratio is 1:1, and the right gap resistance must equal 2 Ω.
3x/(3 + x) = 2 gives 3x = 6 + 2x, so x = 6 Ω.

qs.stem: A soap bubble of surface tension 0.04 N/m is blown to a diameter of 7 cm. If (15000 − x) μJ of work is done in blowing it further to make its diameter 14 cm, then the value of x is ________.
steps: A soap bubble has two surfaces, area 4πR<sup>2</sup> = πD<sup>2</sup> each, so W = 2Tπ(D<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup> − D<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup>).
With π = 22/7: W = 2 × 0.04 × (22/7) × (0.14<sup>2</sup> − 0.07<sup>2</sup>) = 0.08 × 3.1429 × 0.0147 = 3.696×10<sup>−3</sup> J = 3696 μJ.

qs.stem: At 298 K, the mole percentage of N<sub>2</sub>(g) in air is 80%. Water is in equilibrium with air at a pressure of 10 atm. What is the mole fraction of N<sub>2</sub>(g) in water at 298 K? (K<sub>H</sub> for N<sub>2</sub> is 6.5×10<sup>7</sup> mmHg)
steps: Partial pressure of N<sub>2</sub> = 0.80 × 10 atm = 8 atm = 8 × 760 = 6080 mmHg.
Henry's law: p = K<sub>H</sub>·x, so x = 6080/(6.5×10<sup>7</sup>).
x = 9.35×10<sup>−5</sup>.

qs.stem: The wavelength of light absorbed for the following complexes are in the order [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3+</sup> (I); [Co(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3+</sup> (II); [Co(CN)<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3−</sup> (III); [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>(H<sub>2</sub>O)]<sup>3+</sup> (IV); [CoF<sub>6</sub>]<sup>3−</sup> (V)
steps: Spectrochemical series: CN<sup>−</sup> > NH<sub>3</sub> > H<sub>2</sub>O > F<sup>−</sup>, so the splitting Δ<sub>o</sub> follows III > I > IV > II > V (IV has one weaker H<sub>2</sub>O, so it lies between I and II).
Absorbed wavelength is inversely proportional to Δ<sub>o</sub> (λ = hc/Δ<sub>o</sub>).
So λ increases as III < I < IV < II < V.

qs.stem: In the Group analysis of cations, Ba<sup>2+</sup> & Ca<sup>2+</sup> are precipitated respectively as
steps: Ba<sup>2+</sup>, Sr<sup>2+</sup> and Ca<sup>2+</sup> form Group V of cation analysis.
The group reagent is (NH<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> in presence of NH<sub>4</sub>Cl and NH<sub>4</sub>OH.
Both are therefore precipitated as BaCO<sub>3</sub> and CaCO<sub>3</sub> (carbonate & carbonate).

qs.stem: The number of possible tripeptides formed involving alanine (ala), glycine (gly) and valine (val), where no amino acid has been used more than once is:
steps: Each tripeptide uses all three different amino acids once, in a sequence.
Number of different sequences = 3! = 6 (e.g. Ala-Gly-Val, Ala-Val-Gly, Gly-Ala-Val, ...).

qs.stem: The unsaturated ether on acidic hydrolysis produces carbonyl compounds as shown below: CH<sub>3</sub>−CH=CH−O−CH=CH<sub>2</sub> →(H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>) CH<sub>3</sub>−CH<sub>2</sub>−CH=O and O=CH−CH<sub>3</sub>. Based on this, predict the solution/reagent that will help to distinguish 'P' and 'Q' obtained in the following reaction: CH<sub>3</sub>−CH=CH−O−C(CH<sub>3</sub>)=CH<sub>2</sub> →(H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>, Δ) P + Q
steps: Following the given pattern, the CH=CH−O end gives CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CHO (propanal) and the C(CH<sub>3</sub>)=CH<sub>2</sub> end gives CH<sub>3</sub>COCH<sub>3</sub> (acetone).
So P and Q are an aliphatic aldehyde and a ketone.
Fehling solution is reduced (red Cu<sub>2</sub>O) by the aldehyde only, so it distinguishes them. DNP and NaHSO<sub>3</sub> react with both; Lucas reagent is for alcohols.

qs.stem: The wavelength of spectral line obtained in the spectrum of Li<sup>2+</sup> ion, when the transition takes place between two levels whose sum is 4 and difference is 2, is
steps: n<sub>1</sub> + n<sub>2</sub> = 4 and n<sub>2</sub> − n<sub>1</sub> = 2 give n<sub>1</sub> = 1, n<sub>2</sub> = 3.
1/λ = R Z<sup>2</sup>(1/1 − 1/9) = R × 9 × 8/9 = 8R, with R = 1.097×10<sup>7</sup> m<sup>−1</sup>.
λ = 1/(8.78×10<sup>7</sup>) m = 1.14×10<sup>−8</sup> m = 1.14×10<sup>−6</sup> cm.

qs.stem: The correct order of C, N, O and F in terms of second ionisation potential is
steps: The second IE is the energy to remove an electron from M<sup>+</sup>. Configurations of the cations: C<sup>+</sup> 2p<sup>1</sup>, N<sup>+</sup> 2p<sup>2</sup>, O<sup>+</sup> 2p<sup>3</sup> (half-filled), F<sup>+</sup> 2p<sup>4</sup>.
Order of difficulty: half-filled p<sup>3</sup> is highest, then p<sup>4</sup> (higher nuclear charge), then p<sup>2</sup>, then p<sup>1</sup>.
So IE<sub>2</sub>: O > F > N > C, i.e. C < N < F < O.

qs.stem: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The dipole moment of R-CN is greater than R-NC and R-NC can undergo hydrolysis under acidic medium to produce R−C(=O)−OH. Statement II: R-CN hydrolyses under acidic medium to produce a compound which on treatment with SOCl<sub>2</sub>, followed by the addition of NH<sub>3</sub> gives another compound (x). This compound (x) on treatment with NaOCl/NaOH gives a product, that on treatment with CHCl<sub>3</sub>/KOH/Δ produces R-NC. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: Statement I: R-NC has the larger dipole moment, and acid hydrolysis of R-NC gives R-NH<sub>2</sub> + HCOOH, not RCOOH. So I is false.
Statement II: RCN → RCOOH → RCOCl → RCONH<sub>2</sub> (x) → (Hofmann bromamide) RNH<sub>2</sub> → (CHCl<sub>3</sub>/KOH, carbylamine) RNC. All steps valid, so II is true.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

qs.stem: Choose the Incorrect statement
steps: Carbon shows −4 (CH<sub>4</sub>), +2 (CO) and +4 (CO<sub>2</sub>): (1) is correct.
Acidic character of dioxides falls down the group, so CO<sub>2</sub> is the most acidic: (2) is correct; C has no d-orbitals, so max covalency is 4: (3) is correct.
<sup>13</sup>C is stable; the radioactive isotope is <sup>14</sup>C, so (4) is incorrect.
opts: Carbon exhibits negative oxidation states along with +4 and +2.
CO<sub>2</sub> is the most acidic oxide among the dioxides of group of 14 elements.
Carbon cannot exceed its covalency more than four.
Among the isotopes of carbon, <sup>13</sup>C is a radioactive isotope.

qs.stem: 'X' is an oxoanion of the lightest element of group 7 (in the periodic table). The metal is in +6 oxidation state in 'X'. The color of the potassium salt of X is
steps: The lightest group 7 element is Mn.
The oxoanion with Mn in +6 is manganate, MnO<sub>4</sub><sup>2−</sup>.
Its potassium salt K<sub>2</sub>MnO<sub>4</sub> is green (KMnO<sub>4</sub> with Mn(+7) is purple).

qs.stem: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Cross aldol condensation between two different aldehydes will always produce four different products. Statement II: When semicarbazide reacts with a mixture of benzaldehyde and acetophenone under optimum pH, it forms a condensation product with acetophenone only. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: Statement I: a crossed aldol gives four products only if both aldehydes have α-hydrogens; with HCHO or PhCHO (no α-H) fewer products form, so 'always four' is false.
Statement II: the aldehyde is far more reactive towards semicarbazide than a ketone, so benzaldehyde (not acetophenone only) forms the semicarbazone. II is false.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

qs.stem: One mole of Cl<sub>2</sub>(g) was passed into 2 L of cold 2 M KOH solution. After the reaction, the concentrations of Cl<sup>−</sup>, ClO<sup>−</sup> and OH<sup>−</sup> are respectively (assume volume remains constant)
steps: KOH present = 2 L × 2 M = 4 mol. Cold dilute alkali: Cl<sub>2</sub> + 2KOH → KCl + KClO + H<sub>2</sub>O.
1 mol Cl<sub>2</sub> uses 2 mol KOH and gives 1 mol Cl<sup>−</sup> and 1 mol ClO<sup>−</sup>; 2 mol OH<sup>−</sup> remain.
Dividing by 2 L: Cl<sup>−</sup> = 0.5 M, ClO<sup>−</sup> = 0.5 M, OH<sup>−</sup> = 1 M.

qs.stem: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution at temperature T K. At T K, the vapour pressures of pure A and B are 55 and 15 kNm<sup>−2</sup> respectively. What is the mole fraction of A in solution of A and B in equilibrium with a vapour in which the mole fraction of A is 0.8?
steps: y<sub>A</sub>/y<sub>B</sub> = (p<sub>A</sub>°x<sub>A</sub>)/(p<sub>B</sub>°x<sub>B</sub>), with y<sub>A</sub>/y<sub>B</sub> = 0.8/0.2 = 4.
4 = (55/15)(x<sub>A</sub>/x<sub>B</sub>) gives x<sub>A</sub>/x<sub>B</sub> = 60/55 = 12/11.

qs.stem: Pair of species among the following having same bond order as well as paramagnetic character will be
steps: Bond orders: O<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup> = 1.5, O<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup> = 2.5; N<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup> = 2.5, N<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup> = 2.5, N<sub>2</sub><sup>2−</sup> = 2.
Option (2): O<sub>2</sub><sup>+</sup> (15 e<sup>−</sup>) and N<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup> (13 e<sup>−</sup>) both have bond order 2.5 and an odd electron, so both are paramagnetic.
Options (1), (3) pair a 1.5 with a 2.5, and (4) pairs 2.5 with 2, so they fail.

qs.stem: Find out the statements which are not true. A. Resonating structures with more number of covalent bonds and lesser charge separation are more stable. B. In electromeric effect, an unsaturated system shows +E effect with nucleophile and −E effect with electrophile. C. Inductive effect is responsible for high melting point, boiling point and dipole moment of polar compounds. D. The greater the number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms, higher is the heat of hydrogenation. E. Stability of carbanion increases with the increase in s−character of the carbon carrying the negative charge.
steps: A is true (more bonds, less charge separation means more stable). C is true (inductive polarisation causes polarity and its effects). E is true (higher s-character means greater electronegativity of C, stabilising the carbanion).
B is false: with a nucleophile the shift is −E, with an electrophile it is +E (the reverse of what is stated).
D is false: more alkyl groups make the alkene more stable, so heat of hydrogenation is lower. So B and D are not true.

qs.stem: A student has planned to prepare acetanilide from aniline using acetic anhydride. The student has started from 9.3 g of aniline. However, the student has managed to obtain 11 g of dry acetanilide. The % yield of this reaction is :-
steps: Aniline (93 g/mol): 9.3 g = 0.1 mol, giving 0.1 mol acetanilide (135 g/mol) = 13.5 g theoretical.

qs.stem: Given below are two statements: Statement I: There are several conformers for n-butane. Out of those conformers, (X) [Newman projection with both CH<sub>3</sub> groups eclipsed] is the least stable and the most stable conformer is (Y) [Newman projection with the CH<sub>3</sub> groups anti]. Statement II: As the dihedral angle increases, torsional strain decreases from (X) to (Y). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: X has the two CH<sub>3</sub> groups eclipsed (dihedral 0°): maximum steric and torsional strain, so least stable. Y has them anti (180°): minimum strain, most stable. Statement I is true.
Going from X (0°) to Y (180°) the dihedral angle rises and the torsional strain falls, so Statement II is true.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

qs.stem: Grignard reagent RMgBr (P) reacts with water and forms a gas (Q). One gram of Q occupies 1.4 dm<sup>3</sup> at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh ______ g. (Nearest integer)
steps: RMgBr + H<sub>2</sub>O → RH (Q). 1 g occupies 1.4 L at STP, so M = 22.4/1.4 = 16 g/mol, i.e. CH<sub>4</sub>; P = CH<sub>3</sub>MgBr.
CH<sub>3</sub>MgBr + CO<sub>2</sub> then H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup> gives CH<sub>3</sub>COOH (Z), M = 60 g/mol.
0.1 mol × 60 = 6 g.

qs.stem: The half-life of <sup>65</sup>Zn is 245 days. After x days, 75% of original activity remained. The value of x in days is ______ (Nearest integer) (Given: log 3 = 0.4771 and log 2 = 0.3010)
steps: Decay is first order: k = 0.693/245 and N/N<sub>0</sub> = 0.75, so t = (1/k) ln(4/3).
t ≈ 101.7, i.e. 102 days.

qs.stem: A chromium complex with a formula CrCl<sub>3</sub>·6H<sub>2</sub>O has a spin only magnetic moment value of 3.87 BM and its solution conductivity corresponds to 1:2 electrolyte. 2.75 g of the complex solution was initially passed through a cation exchanger. The solution obtained after the process was reacted with excess of AgNO<sub>3</sub>. The amount of AgCl formed in the above process is _______ g. (Nearest integer) [Given: Molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup> Cr : 52; Cl : 35.5, Ag : 108, O : 16, H : 1]
steps: Cr<sup>3+</sup> (d<sup>3</sup>) gives 3.87 BM; a 1:2 electrolyte means [Cr(H<sub>2</sub>O)<sub>5</sub>Cl]Cl<sub>2</sub>·H<sub>2</sub>O. Molar mass = 52 + 106.5 + 108 = 266.5 g/mol, so 2.75 g = 0.0103 mol.
The cation exchanger removes the complex cation (the coordinated Cl goes with it) and leaves the 2 ionic Cl<sup>−</sup> as HCl: 0.0103 × 2 = 0.0206 mol Cl<sup>−</sup>.
AgCl = 0.0206 × 143.5 = 2.96 g ≈ 3 g.

qs.stem: 0.25 g of an organic compound 'A' containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen was analysed using the combustion method. There was an increase in mass of CaCl<sub>2</sub> tube and potash tube at the end of the experiment. The amount was found to be 0.15 g and 0.1837 g, respectively. The percentage of oxygen in compound A is __________ %. (Nearest integer) (Given: molar mass in g mol<sup>−1</sup> H : 1, C : 12, O : 16)
steps: CaCl<sub>2</sub> absorbs H<sub>2</sub>O (0.15 g) and the potash tube absorbs CO<sub>2</sub> (0.1837 g).

qs.stem: Molar conductivity of a weak acid HQ of concentration 0.18 M was found to be 1/30 of the molar conductivity of another weak acid HZ with concentration of 0.02 M. If λ°<sub>Q<sup>−</sup></sub> happened to be equal with λ°<sub>Z<sup>−</sup></sub>, then the difference of the pK<sub>a</sub> values of the two weak acids (pK<sub>a</sub>(HQ) − pK<sub>a</sub>(HZ)) is _______ (Nearest integer). [Given: degree of dissociation (α) << 1 for both weak acids, λ° : limiting molar conductivity of ions]
steps: Same ionic limiting conductivities (H<sup>+</sup> common, Q<sup>−</sup> = Z<sup>−</sup>) means equal Λ°, so α ∝ Λ<sub>m</sub> and α(HQ)/α(HZ) = 1/30.
pK<sub>a</sub>(HQ) − pK<sub>a</sub>(HZ) = −log(1/100) = 2.
